title: Local Bodies & Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution, placed among the Directive Principles of State Policy, directs the State to organise village panchayats and endow them with the powers needed to function as units of self-government?
questions.e: Article 40 in Part IV is the Gandhian directive on which the 73rd Amendment later built constitutional Panchayats. Article 46 concerns the interests of SC/ST and weaker sections, Article 39 the distribution of resources, and Article 243 is only the definitions article of Part IX.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj
questions.h: Gandhi's village swaraj sits at 40: four-oh, village-O.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:
1. It inserted Part IX, containing Articles 243 to 243-O, into the Constitution.
2. It added the Eleventh Schedule listing 29 functional items for Panchayats.
3. It came into force on 1 June 1993.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) and the Eleventh Schedule (29 items) came through the 73rd Amendment, which took effect on 24 April 1993, hence National Panchayati Raj Day. The date of 1 June 1993 belongs to the 74th Amendment on Municipalities.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj
questions.h: Village first on 24 April, town later on 1 June.

questions.q:
Match the following committees with their key recommendation on Panchayati Raj:
List-I (Committee)
A. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
B. Ashok Mehta Committee
C. G.V.K. Rao Committee
List-II (Recommendation)
1. Three-tier system of democratic decentralisation at village, block and district levels
2. Two-tier system of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat
3. Post of District Development Commissioner; Panchayati Raj called 'grass without roots'
questions.e: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) gave the three-tier model, Ashok Mehta (1977) shrank it to two tiers with the district as the focus, and G.V.K. Rao (1985) criticised bureaucratisation and proposed a District Development Commissioner. The tiers shrank from three to two because the block tier had failed to deliver.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj
questions.h: Mehta 57 = three tiers; Mehta 77 = two tiers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Panchayats under Part IX of the Constitution:
1. The minimum age for being a Panchayat member is 25 years, the same as for a State Legislative Assembly.
2. A Panchayat continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting.
3. If a Panchayat is dissolved before its term ends, an election must be completed within six months of the dissolution.
4. A State must constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level irrespective of its population.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 243-F fixes the minimum age at 21 years, not 25, and Article 243-B(2) lets States with a population not exceeding 20 lakh skip the intermediate tier. Statements 2 and 3 follow Article 243-E, which also says that a body elected after premature dissolution serves only the remainder of the original term.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Statement-I: Even after the 73rd and 74th Amendments, the actual powers and functions of Panchayats and municipalities depend on State legislation.
Statement-II: Articles 243-G and 243-W provide that the State Legislature 'may' by law endow these bodies with powers and authority, and 'local government' is an entry in the State List.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Because local government is State List entry 5 and the endowment articles use the word 'may', devolution of the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedule subjects is a State choice, not a constitutional compulsion.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a compulsory (mandatory) provision of the 73rd Amendment Act?
o: Reservation of not less than one-third of seats for women
Constitution of a State Finance Commission every five years
Constitution of a State Election Commission for Panchayat elections
Reservation of seats for backward classes in Panchayats
questions.e: Reservation for backward classes is voluntary: Article 243-D(6) says the State Legislature 'may' provide it. Women's reservation, the State Finance Commission and the State Election Commission are all compulsory features.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Election Commission and State Finance Commission for Panchayats:
1. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds applicable to a High Court judge.
2. The Governor must constitute a State Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats.
3. The recommendations of the State Finance Commission are binding on the State Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 243-K and 243-I give the Election Commissioner High Court judge-like security and require a Finance Commission every five years. Its recommendations are advisory: they are laid before the Legislature with an action-taken memorandum and are not binding.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the bar on court interference in Panchayat electoral matters under Article 243-O:
1. The validity of a law relating to delimitation of Panchayat constituencies or allotment of seats cannot be questioned in any court.
2. No Panchayat election can be questioned except by an election petition presented to the authority and in the manner provided by State law.
3. Only the Supreme Court can hear Panchayat election petitions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 243-O mirrors Article 329 for Parliament: delimitation and seat-allotment laws are immune, and elections can be challenged only through an election petition as State law provides. Nothing makes the Supreme Court the forum for Panchayat disputes.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects is included in the Twelfth Schedule but NOT in the Eleventh Schedule?
questions.e: Fire services is a Twelfth Schedule (urban) function. Libraries, markets and fairs, and social forestry are Eleventh Schedule items for Panchayats, with the urban counterpart of forestry being 'urban forestry'.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Municipalities

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 74th Amendment:
1. Ward Committees are to be constituted in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more.
2. A Metropolitan Planning Committee is to be constituted for a metropolitan area with a population of five lakh or more.
3. A Nagar Panchayat is constituted for an area in transition from a rural area to an urban area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 243-S (Ward Committees, three lakh) and Article 243-Q (Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area) are correctly stated. A metropolitan area under Article 243-P and 243-ZE needs a population of ten lakh or more, not five lakh.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Municipalities
questions.h: 3 lakh = Ward committee; 10 lakh = Metro committee.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about urban local bodies in India:
1. Cantonment Boards are administered by the Union Ministry of Defence.
2. A Notified Area Committee is a fully elected statutory body.
3. A Town Area Committee is a semi-municipal authority created by a separate State Act for a small town.
4. Port Trusts are created by an Act of Parliament to manage and protect ports.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A Notified Area Committee is created by a government notification and all its members are nominated, so statement 2 is wrong. Cantonment Boards (Cantonments Act, 2006), Town Area Committees and Port Trusts are described correctly.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Municipalities

questions.q:
Arrange the following Panchayati Raj committees in chronological order:
1. Ashok Mehta Committee
2. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
3. L.M. Singhvi Committee
4. Thungon Committee
questions.e: The sequence is Balwant Rai Mehta (1957), Ashok Mehta (1977), L.M. Singhvi (1986) and P.K. Thungon (1988). Both Singhvi and Thungon pushed for constitutional status, which finally came in 1992.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : Subject
1. Article 243-A : Gram Sabha
2. Article 243-D : Duration of Panchayats
3. Article 243-I : Constitution of State Finance Commission
4. Article 243-K : Elections to the Panchayats
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Article 243-D deals with reservation of seats; the duration of Panchayats is in Article 243-E. The other three pairs are correct.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Statement-I: Elections to Panchayats in a State are conducted by an authority independent of the Election Commission of India.
Statement-II: Article 243-K vests superintendence, direction and control of Panchayat elections in the State Election Commission, a body distinct from the Election Commission of India.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Both are correct and the second is the reason for the first. Article 324 covers elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President, while local body polls go to the State Election Commission.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q: The Finance Commission is required to recommend measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities on the basis of the recommendations of which body?
o: The State Finance Commission of that State
questions.e: Article 280(3)(bb) and (c), inserted by the 73rd and 74th Amendments, link the Union Finance Commission to the State Finance Commission's report. The SFC studies local needs, and the Union FC then suggests how the State's pool can be topped up.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Finance Commission

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of local self-government in India:
1. Rajasthan was the first State to establish a Panchayati Raj system, inaugurated at Nagaur in 1959.
2. Lord Mayo's Resolution of 1870 is regarded as the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government in India.
3. Under the Government of India Act, 1919, local self-government became a transferred subject.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 'Magna Carta' label belongs to Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882, which promoted elected local boards; Mayo's 1870 Resolution was about financial decentralisation. Rajasthan's Nagaur launch and the 1919 transfer of local self-government to Indian ministers are correct.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj; Spectrum, Modern India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the District Planning Committee under Article 243-ZD:
1. At least four-fifths of its members are elected by the elected members of the district-level Panchayat and the Municipalities in the district, from among themselves.
2. Its Chairperson must be the District Collector.
3. It consolidates the plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities into a draft development plan for the whole district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The composition is fixed by State law, and the Constitution does not name the Collector as Chairperson. The Committee's job under Article 243-ZD is precisely to merge rural and urban plans into one district plan.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Municipalities

questions.q: A State has a population of 15 lakh. Which of the following correctly describes the tiers of Panchayats it must constitute under Part IX?
o: All three tiers, without any exception
Village level and district level; the intermediate level is optional
Village and intermediate levels only, with the district level optional
questions.e: Article 243-B(2) permits a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh to skip the intermediate tier, so 15 lakh qualifies. The village and district tiers remain mandatory.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of a Municipality under Article 243-R:
1. All members are chosen only by direct election from territorial constituencies called wards.
2. Persons with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration may be nominated, but they have no right to vote in meetings.
3. State law may provide for representation of MPs and MLAs whose constituencies fall wholly or partly in the municipal area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 243-R permits nominated experts without voting rights and representation of legislators, so not all members are directly elected. Statement 1's word 'only' makes it wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Municipalities

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation in Municipalities under Article 243-T:
1. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population in the municipal area.
2. Not less than one-third of the total seats, including those reserved for SC/ST women, are reserved for women.
3. Reservation for backward classes in Municipalities is compulsory.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 follow Article 243-T. Backward-class reservation is left to the State Legislature, which 'may' provide for it, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Municipalities

questions.q: Under Article 243-K, who determines the conditions of service and tenure of office of the State Election Commissioner, subject to any law made by the State Legislature?
o: The Chief Election Commissioner of India
questions.e: Article 243-K(2) lets the Governor fix them by rule, subject to State law. The Governor also appoints the Commissioner, and the Commissioner's conditions cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding membership of a Panchayat under Article 243-F:
1. A person who has attained the age of 21 years is not disqualified merely on the ground of being below 25 years.
2. A person is disqualified if disqualified under any law for the time being in force for elections to the Legislature of the State concerned.
3. Questions of disqualification of Panchayat members are decided by the Election Commission of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 243-F lowers the age floor to 21 and borrows State Legislature disqualifications, but any disqualification dispute goes to the authority State law specifies, not the ECI.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q: The provisions of Part IX (Panchayats) may be applied to a Union Territory by
o: A public notification of the President, subject to exceptions and modifications
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha under Article 249
Ratification by half of the State Legislatures
An order of the Supreme Court
questions.e: Article 243-L lets the President direct, by public notification, that the Part applies to a Union Territory or part of it with such exceptions and modifications as specified. No special ratification or Rajya Sabha resolution is needed.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 functional items for Municipalities.
Statement-II: Article 243-W makes it obligatory for the State Legislature to devolve all 18 subjects on Municipalities.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Twelfth Schedule, inserted by the 74th Amendment, indeed lists 18 items. Article 243-W only says the Legislature 'may' endow Municipalities with powers, so devolution is not obligatory.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Municipalities

questions.q:
How many of the following subjects are included in the Eleventh Schedule?
1. Libraries
2. Markets and fairs
3. Burial grounds and cremation grounds
4. Fuel and fodder
questions.e: Libraries, markets and fairs, and fuel and fodder are Eleventh Schedule subjects. Burials and cremation grounds belong to the Twelfth Schedule for urban bodies.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Panchayati Raj

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes?
questions.e: Article 244(1) brings the Fifth Schedule and Article 244(2) the Sixth Schedule. Article 244A permits an autonomous State in Assam, Article 275 provides grants, and Article 342 lists the Scheduled Tribes.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fifth Schedule:
1. The President declares Scheduled Areas after consulting the Governor of the State concerned.
2. A Tribes Advisory Council has not more than 20 members, of whom, as nearly as may be, three-fourths are representatives of Scheduled Tribes in the State Legislative Assembly.
3. The Governor must submit a report on the administration of Scheduled Areas to the President every five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Para 6 (declaration after consulting the Governor) and Para 4 (Tribes Advisory Council) are correctly stated. Para 3 requires the Governor to report annually, or whenever the President requires, not every five years.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Under the Fifth Schedule, consider the following statements about the Governor's powers in Scheduled Areas:
1. The Governor may direct that a particular Act of Parliament shall not apply to a Scheduled Area or shall apply with modifications.
2. The Governor may make regulations prohibiting or restricting transfer of land by or among members of Scheduled Tribes.
3. Such regulations may be made without consulting the Tribes Advisory Council.
4. Such regulations take effect without the assent of the President.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Para 5 gives the Governor both powers, but regulations under it are made only after consulting the Tribes Advisory Council and need the President's assent. Statements 3 and 4 therefore fail.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Match the following Autonomous District Councils with their States:
List-I (Council)
A. Garo Hills
B. Chakma
C. Dima Hasao
D. Tripura Tribal Areas
List-II (State)
1. Assam
2. Meghalaya
3. Mizoram
4. Tripura
questions.e: Garo Hills is in Meghalaya, Chakma (with Lai and Mara) in Mizoram, Dima Hasao (formerly North Cachar Hills) in Assam and the Tripura Tribal Areas ADC in Tripura. All four States are covered by the Sixth Schedule.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 was enacted by Parliament rather than being left to the States.
Statement-II: Article 243-M(4)(b) empowers Parliament to extend Part IX to Scheduled Areas subject to such exceptions and modifications as it specifies.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Part IX does not apply to Scheduled Areas on its own (Article 243-M), but Parliament may extend it by law. PESA, 1996 is that law, passed after the Bhuria Committee's report.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996:
1. Recommendation of the Gram Sabha or the Panchayat at the appropriate level is mandatory before granting a prospecting licence or mining lease for minor minerals.
2. The prior consent of the Gram Sabha is required for every acquisition of land for development projects.
3. The offices of Chairpersons of Panchayats at all levels are reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PESA requires only that the Gram Sabha or the appropriate Panchayat be consulted before land acquisition; it does not require consent. The mandatory recommendation for minor mineral concessions and the ST reservation of all Chairperson offices are correct.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 was based on the recommendations of a committee chaired by
questions.e: The Committee of MPs and experts on Panchayati Raj in Scheduled Areas was headed by Dileep Singh Bhuria. U.N. Dhebar headed the 1960 Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes Commission, and Ashok Mehta the 1977 Panchayati Raj committee.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006:
1. The cut-off date for recognising the forest rights of Scheduled Tribes is 13 December 2005.
2. Other traditional forest dwellers must have resided in the forest land for at least three generations (75 years) before the cut-off date.
3. Individual forest rights over land in occupation are limited to ten hectares.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act fixes 13 December 2005 as the cut-off and asks non-tribal forest dwellers for three generations of residence. The ceiling on individual occupation is four hectares, not ten.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
1. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for its implementation.
2. Bamboo is included in the definition of minor forest produce.
3. It provides for habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.
4. It applies only to Fifth Schedule Areas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. The Act applies to forest lands across the country wherever Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers live, not only in Fifth Schedule Areas.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: Which one of the following sets correctly lists States where the Constitution provides for a Minister in charge of tribal welfare?
o: Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Gujarat and Rajasthan
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
questions.e: The proviso to Article 164(1), as amended by the 94th Amendment Act, 2006, names these four States. Bihar was dropped after Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh were carved out.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Enactment of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act
2. Constitutional status to a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
3. Report of the Dhebar Commission
4. Enactment of the Forest Rights Act
questions.e: The order is the Dhebar Commission (1960-61), PESA (1996), the 89th Amendment creating a separate Scheduled Tribes commission (2003) and the Forest Rights Act (2006).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sixth Schedule:
1. A District Council can have up to 30 members, of whom not more than four are nominated by the Governor.
2. Elected members of a District Council hold office for five years unless the Council is sooner dissolved.
3. A District Council can make laws on the management of reserved forests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The composition and five-year term are as laid down in Para 2. The Council's law-making power covers forests other than reserved forests, which stay with the State.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sixth Schedule:
1. It is linked to Articles 244(2) and 275(1).
2. It applies to the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
3. The Governor may create, alter the boundaries or change the names of autonomous districts.
4. Acts of Parliament and the State Legislature apply to autonomous districts in full force without any modification.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong because laws of Parliament and the State apply to autonomous areas only if the specified authority so directs, and often with modifications or exceptions.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Statement-I: A Tribes Advisory Council can be established in a State having Scheduled Tribes but no Scheduled Areas.
Statement-II: In such a case, the Governor of the State has the power to establish the Council on his own.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Under the Fifth Schedule such a Council can be set up if the President so directs, so the first statement is right. The second is wrong because the initiative lies with the President, not the Governor.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs):
1. The Dhebar Commission's findings of unequal development among tribal groups led to a separate category of primitive tribal groups, later renamed PVTGs.
2. They are identified on criteria that include a pre-agricultural level of technology and a stagnant or declining population.
3. The list of PVTGs is notified by the Governor of the State in consultation with the Tribes Advisory Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The category grew out of the Dhebar Commission's finding that some groups lagged far behind other tribes, and the identification criteria include pre-agricultural technology, low literacy and a stagnant or declining population. PVTGs are identified by the Central Government and the Governor has no such role.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: Which Article provides for grants-in-aid from the Union to States for promoting the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas?
questions.e: Article 275(1) charges such grants on the Consolidated Fund of India. Article 339 deals with control of the Union over administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, while Article 282 covers discretionary grants.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST):
1. It was established under Article 338A by the 65th Amendment Act.
2. It consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other Members.
3. The list of Scheduled Tribes of a State is specified by the President after consulting the Governor, and can be altered only by Parliament by law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 338A was inserted by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003, which split the earlier joint SC/ST commission created in 1990 by the 65th Amendment. Composition and the Article 342 procedure are correctly stated.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: Article 244A, which allows the creation of an autonomous State comprising certain tribal areas of Assam, was inserted by which Amendment?
questions.e: The 22nd Amendment enabled Meghalaya to become an autonomous State within Assam in 1970 before full Statehood in 1972. The 13th Amendment gave Nagaland Article 371A, and the 7th reorganised States.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: In 2013, in the case concerning bauxite mining in the Niyamgiri hills, the Supreme Court directed that which bodies should decide whether the mining would affect the religious and cultural rights of the Dongria Kondh?
questions.e: The Court asked the Odisha villages to hold Gram Sabhas under the Forest Rights Act, which then rejected the project. The case showed Gram Sabha consent acting as a real check on mining.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: Which Supreme Court judgment (1997) held that the transfer of land in Scheduled Areas by the government to private non-tribal entities for mining was void?
o: Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India
Lafarge Umiam Mining v. Union of India
Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh
questions.e: Samatha read the Fifth Schedule and the State land transfer regulations to forbid leasing tribal land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals. The other cases concern dams, forests and forest clearance respectively.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : Provision
1. Article 244A : Autonomous State within Assam
2. Article 275(1) : Grants-in-aid for tribal welfare
3. Article 338A : Commission to report on the administration of Scheduled Areas
4. Article 342 : Specification of Scheduled Castes
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are right. Article 338A is the NCST, while the commission to report on Scheduled Areas is under Article 339; Article 342 specifies Scheduled Tribes, whereas Scheduled Castes are under Article 341.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
How many of the following States have Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule?
1. Himachal Pradesh
2. Gujarat
3. Tripura
4. Maharashtra
questions.e: Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra have Fifth Schedule areas, which now exist in ten States. Tripura is governed by the Sixth Schedule.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the judicial powers of District Councils under the Sixth Schedule:
1. They can constitute village councils or courts to try suits and cases between parties who are all Scheduled Tribes, other than cases punishable with death or imprisonment of five years or more.
2. The jurisdiction of the High Court over such suits and cases is as specified by the Governor.
3. Their judicial powers extend to all persons in the district irrespective of tribe.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The tribal courts handle disputes among Scheduled Tribes and are limited to less serious cases, with the Governor deciding the High Court's role. They do not try non-tribals.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q: The 'Tribal Panchsheel', a policy approach emphasising tribal development along their own genius and respect for their rights in land and forests, is associated with
questions.e: Nehru, influenced by Verrier Elwin, advocated a middle path between isolation and forced assimilation. Ghurye is known for the opposing 'backward Hindus' view of assimilation.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas

questions.q:
Which of the statements below about the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 are correct?
1. State legislation on Panchayats in Scheduled Areas may be inconsistent with the customary law and traditional management practices of communities.
2. Gram Sabha is competent to prevent alienation of land of Scheduled Tribes and to take action to restore unlawfully alienated land.
3. Panchayats have the power to enforce prohibition or to regulate and restrict the sale and consumption of any intoxicant.
questions.e: Section 4 of PESA requires State laws to be in consonance with customary law, social and religious practices and traditional management of community resources, so statement 1 is wrong. The land-alienation and intoxicant powers are correct.
